newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine June gov't deficit rises to $172 mln.
newsitem.headline: Argentine June gov't deficit rises to $172 mln.

text.p: Argentina's central government deficit was $172 million in June, compared to a $68 million surplus in the same month last year, Finance Under Secretary Pablo Guidotti said Monday.
Guidotti said that the government thought Argentina's first half deficit would be $50 million below the target it has agreed with the International Monetary Fund.
Argentina's targets with the IMF are for a $1.4 billion deficit in the first half, not including spending on items including a fund to retrain or compensate former state employees.
Treasury income rose to $1.36 billion in June, up almost $51 million from the same month last year, while spending rose by $186 million to $1.45 billion.
Guidotti added that the government is studying the possibility of issuing bonds in Italian lire in July, but that conditions are also favorable for dollar issues.
Spending will rise by $1.2 billion in 1998, due to higher interest payments, but the economy will grow faster than spending, Guidotti said.
He added that the government aims to increase the national education budget by $170 million, to reach a 1992 target of doubling eduction spending from that year's levels.
